questions.question: What is a mixture?

answers.a: A substance that consists of one type of molecule
answers.b: A substance with a fixed boiling point
answers.c: A substance made up of more than one kind of molecule
answers.d: A substance made up of one kind of atom

questions.question: What is a pure substance?

answers.a: A substance that is not a compound
answers.b: A substance without colour or smell
answers.c: A substance made up of several kinds of molecules
answers.d: A substance that consists of one type of molecule

questions.question: How can you recognise a pure substance from its boiling point?

answers.a: The boiling point differs from sample to sample
answers.b: The boiling point is fixed and stays the same during boiling
answers.c: The temperature keeps rising during boiling
answers.d: The substance has no boiling point

questions.question: What are the separation methods in BAEDFIA?

answers.a: Settling, decanting, decomposition, drying, filtration, melting, adsorption
answers.b: Settling, reading off, extraction, drying, filtration, evaporation, cooling
answers.c: Breaking, decanting, electrolysis, distillation, filtration, evaporation, diluting
answers.d: Bezinken, Afgieten, Extraheren, Destilleren, Filtreren, Indampen, Adsorberen (Dutch: settling, decanting, extraction, distillation, filtration, evaporation, adsorption)

questions.question: Which method do you use to separate sand from water?
What difference between substances is filtration based on?

answers.b: The difference in density of the liquids

questions.question: What is left behind on the filter: the residue or the filtrate?
What passes through the filter: the residue or the filtrate?
What is a mixture of a solid and a liquid, in which the solid does not dissolve, called?
What is a mixture of two liquids that do not mix, such as oil and water, called?
How do you separate a suspension of chalk in water?
How do you separate oil from water in an emulsion that has been left to stand for a while?

answers.d: By decanting or with a separating funnel, because oil floats on water

questions.question: What difference is settling and decanting based on?
How do you get salt out of salt water if you do not need to keep the water?
How do you turn salt water back into pure water that you keep?
On which difference between substances is distillation based?
What is the substance called that becomes liquid in the condenser during distillation and is collected?
What is the condenser used for in a distillation?

answers.a: To let the vapour condense back into a liquid

questions.question: Alcohol boils at 78 °C and water at 100 °C. Which substance distils over first if you distil the mixture?

answers.a: Alcohol, because it has the lowest boiling point
answers.b: Water, because it has the highest boiling point
answers.d: Neither, the mixture does not boil

questions.question: Substance A boils at 65 °C and substance B at 110 °C. You heat the mixture slowly to 80 °C. What has distilled over then?

answers.b: An equal mixture of A and B

questions.question: Why is distillation not a good way to separate sand from water?

answers.a: Sand has the same boiling point as water
answers.d: Sand does not dissolve, so filtering is much simpler

questions.question: What is it called when you separate a substance from a mixture using a solvent in which only that substance dissolves?
Which example is extraction?

answers.b: Getting salt out of sea water by evaporation
answers.c: Making tea: the flavour compounds dissolve in the hot water

questions.question: What difference is extraction based on?
What is it called when substances are separated because a solid holds on to the substances differently, as in a carbon filter?
What do you use to remove odours or dyes from a mixture?
How do you get iron powder out of a mixture of iron powder and sulfur powder?
How do you get sugar out of sugar water if you do not need to keep the water?
Which method do you use to separate sand and salt? Sand does not dissolve in water, salt does.

answers.c: Add water, filter and evaporate the filtrate

questions.question: You filter a mixture of chalk and water. The filtrate is clear. Is the filtrate a pure substance?

answers.a: No, there is still chalk in it
answers.b: Yes, filtering always gives a pure substance
answers.c: Not necessarily, something may still be dissolved in the water
answers.d: Yes, because it is clear and therefore pure water

questions.question: What is it called when coloured substances are separated on paper using a solvent?
Which two steps belong to separating a mixture of sand, salt and water, in the correct order?

answers.c: First filter, then evaporate the filtrate
